To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the novel ACADM gene cDNA sequence variation c.145C> G is a missense mutation, which causes a substitution of glutamine by glutamate at position Q24 of the mature enzyme; (2) it is the first time that this mutation is reported; (3) it is located on the same allele as the common c. 985A>G mutation; and (4) it causes a mild MCADD.

the ACADM gene mutation c.145C > G is associated with a mild MCADD and that this mutation is responsible, in combination with the common c.985A > G mutation, for a phenotype that is similar to the mild MCADD phenotypes detected by MS/ MS newborn screening.
a novel c. 145C>G mutation in the ACADM gene causes a mild MCADD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel mutation in the ACADM gene and its associated clinical and biochemical findings.
the clinical, biochemical and molecular genetic aspects of a case of MCADD with a novel mutation in exon 3 of the ACADM (Q24E) associated with the c.985A> G mutation in exon 4.
the identification of a novel ACADM mutation, the first report of this mutation and its association with the common c985A>G mutation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient is compound heterozygote for the c.985A >G and the novel c.145 C > G mutations in the ACADM gene.
a novel c. 145C>G mutation in the ACADM gene is associated with mild MCADD and that this mutation is not a common polymorphism.
the patient has MCADD, with mild phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first report of the novel ACADM gene mutation c.145C> G and that this mutation associated with heterozygous c.985A> G is responsible for a typical MCADD phenotype.
the c.145C> G mutation is a novel mutation and the first report for it.
the novel ACADM c.145C> G mutation (Q24E) is a rare but important cause of mild MCADD and that this mutation may be associated with the c.985A> G mutation on the other allele.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical presentation of MCADD is not always typical, even when the genotype is typical.
the clinical phenotype of patients with genotypes of mild MCAD should not be ignored.
the clinical presentation of a patient with MCADD should not be dismissed based solely on the absence of glycine conjugate excretion.
